_note: One mystery a week for thirty-six weeks at every grade that has been written. Each case is a short story, a question, the suspects with what the text says about each, and the teacher answer with its proof quotes. A mystery is a claim-and-evidence task in disguise, which is why it sits beside the writing step and uses the same frame. The feeder hangs from a branch two feet from the trunk. Scratches run down the pole and along the branch above the feeder. A squirrel can jump four feet from a standing start. The class moved the feeder six feet out, away from every branch, and it lasted twelve days.
cases.question: What emptied the feeder?

suspects.why: scratches on the branch, and it can jump four feet
no seed lay on the ground beneath it
the same mix the class always buys

cases.answer: A squirrel reached the feeder from the branch.
proof: “Scratches run down the pole and along the branch above the feeder.”
“A squirrel can jump four feet from a standing start.”
clears: A leak: “No seed lay on the ground beneath it.”
Bad seed: “The seed was the same mix the class always buys.”
cases.explain: Moving the feeder six feet out made it last twelve days. Because a squirrel can jump four feet and left scratches on the branch above, it was reaching the feeder from the tree.

cases.title: The Case of the Gritty Cocoa
cases.story: The cocoa at the winter party was gritty at the bottom of every cup. The mix was fresh. The milk was cold from the fridge. The recipe says to stir the powder into a little hot milk first. Room 8 poured all the cold milk in at once and stirred twice. Room 9 followed the recipe and had no grit. Cocoa powder does not dissolve in cold liquid. A spoonful of the leftover grit dissolved at once in hot water.
cases.question: Why was the cocoa gritty?

suspects.why: powder does not dissolve in cold liquid
the mix was fresh
a spoonful dissolved at once in hot water

cases.answer: The cold milk left the cocoa powder undissolved.
proof: “Room 8 poured all the cold milk in at once and stirred twice.”
“Cocoa powder does not dissolve in cold liquid.”
clears: Old mix: “The mix was fresh.”
The grit: “A spoonful of the leftover grit dissolved at once in hot water.”
cases.explain: Room 9 followed the recipe and had no grit. Because Room 8 poured cold milk in all at once, and cocoa powder does not dissolve in cold liquid, the powder sank to the bottom.

cases.title: The Case of the Torn Valentines
cases.story: Twenty valentines went into the class mailbox and came out with torn corners. The mailbox is a cardboard box with a slot cut in the lid. The slot is three inches wide. Most of the envelopes are four inches across. Jamal pushed his through and the corner caught on the cardboard. Ms. Reyes had taped the slot edges, but the tape had peeled back. Every tear is on a corner, and all the tears face the same way.
cases.question: What tore the valentines?

suspects.why: the slot is three inches, the envelopes are four
all the tears face the same way
every tear is on a corner

cases.answer: The narrow slot tore the corners off the envelopes.
proof: “The slot is three inches wide.”
“Jamal pushed his through and the corner caught on the cardboard.”
clears: A student: “all the tears face the same way.”
A mouse: “Every tear is on a corner”
cases.explain: All the tears are on corners and face the same way, which a hand or a mouse would not do. Because the slot is three inches wide and the envelopes are four inches across, every corner caught.

cases.title: The Case of the Quiet Volcano
cases.story: The science fair volcano fizzed at home and did nothing on stage. Mia used the same baking soda from the same box. The vinegar bottle on stage had been open since the last fair. Vinegar loses its strength once the bottle stays open. A fresh bottle made the model erupt over the table. The model itself had no cracks and the crater was clear. Mia poured the same amount both times. She measured it with the same cup.
cases.question: Why did the volcano not erupt on stage?

suspects.why: the bottle had been open since the last fair
the same box she used at home
no cracks and the crater was clear

cases.answer: The old vinegar had lost its strength.
proof: “The vinegar bottle on stage had been open since the last fair.”
“Vinegar loses its strength once the bottle stays open.”
clears: The baking soda: “Mia used the same baking soda from the same box.”
The model: “The model itself had no cracks and the crater was clear.”
cases.explain: A fresh bottle made the model erupt over the table. Because the stage bottle had been open since the last fair, the vinegar had lost its strength.

cases.title: The Case of the Crooked Crown
cases.story: The paper crown for the play sat straight at dress rehearsal and tipped on opening night. Nobody had bent it, because it was kept flat in a box. The crown is held on with two bobby pins. On opening night Eli wore it over his costume wig. The wig is an inch thicker than his own hair. The pins no longer reached his hair at all. The crown sat on top of the wig instead of down in his hair.
cases.question: Why did the crown tip on opening night?

suspects.why: an inch thicker, so the pins no longer reached his hair
it was kept flat in a box
it is held on with two bobby pins

cases.answer: The wig held the crown too high for the pins to reach hair.
proof: “The wig is an inch thicker than his own hair.”
“The pins no longer reached his hair at all.”
clears: Bending: “it was kept flat in a box.”
Missing pins: “The crown is held on with two bobby pins.”
cases.explain: The crown sat straight at dress rehearsal, when Eli wore no wig. Because the wig is an inch thicker than his hair, the two pins could not reach hair and the crown tipped.

cases.title: The Case of the Silent Pedal
cases.story: The music room piano held its notes all year and stopped on Monday. The keys all sound. The damper pedal goes down and springs back up. Mr. Okafor looked underneath and found the pedal rod resting beside its slot instead of inside it. The piano had been rolled across the room on Friday for the concert. Nothing was dropped and nobody forced the pedal. A rod can shake loose when a piano is moved. He set the rod back in its slot and the notes held again.
cases.question: Why did the piano stop holding its notes?

suspects.why: found resting beside its slot, and the piano was moved
nothing was dropped and nobody forced the pedal
the keys all sound

cases.answer: The pedal rod had shaken loose out of its slot.
proof: “Mr. Okafor looked underneath and found the pedal rod resting beside its slot instead of inside it.”
“A rod can shake loose when a piano is moved.”
clears: Dropping: “Nothing was dropped and nobody forced the pedal.”
A broken key: “The keys all sound.”
cases.explain: He set the rod back in its slot and the notes held again. Because the piano was rolled across the room on Friday, the rod had shaken out of its slot.

cases.title: The Case of the Diving Kite
cases.story: Maya's kite flew well in March and dove straight down in April. The sail has no tears and the strings are even. She flew it from the same field both times. In April she had tied on a shorter tail to make it look neater. A kite's tail keeps the nose pointed up into the wind. Her friend's kite, with its full tail, flew fine beside hers. Maya tied the long tail back on and the kite climbed.
cases.question: Why did the kite dive?

suspects.why: a tail holds the nose up, and a full tail flew fine beside it
the sail has no tears
she flew it from the same field both times

cases.answer: The shorter tail let the kite's nose drop.
proof: “In April she had tied on a shorter tail to make it look neater.”
“A kite's tail keeps the nose pointed up into the wind.”
clears: A torn sail: “The sail has no tears and the strings are even.”
The field: “She flew it from the same field both times.”
cases.explain: Maya tied the long tail back on and the kite climbed. Because the shorter tail could not hold the nose up into the wind, the kite dove.

cases.title: The Case of the Wilted Shamrocks
cases.story: Room 9 grew shamrocks on two windowsills from the same packet of seed. The south window plants are pale and drooping. The north window plants are green. Both pots were watered on the same days with the same cup. The south sill sits above the heater vent, which has run since February. A thermometer on the south sill reads eighty-four degrees. The packet says shamrocks want a cool room. The soil in the south pot was dry an hour after watering.
cases.question: Why are the south window shamrocks wilting?

suspects.why: the sill reads eighty-four, and the packet wants a cool room
both pots were watered on the same days with the same cup
both came from the same packet

cases.answer: Heat from the vent dried the south pot out.
proof: “A thermometer on the south sill reads eighty-four degrees.”
“The packet says shamrocks want a cool room.”
clears: Water: “Both pots were watered on the same days with the same cup.”
Bad seed: “from the same packet of seed.”
cases.explain: The north window plants are green on the same water and the same seed. Because the south sill sits above the heater vent and reads eighty-four degrees, that soil was dry an hour after watering.

cases.title: The Case of the Hallway Puddle
cases.story: A puddle appears outside the art room every Tuesday and never on other days. The roof above it was replaced in August and does not leak. The drinking fountain is forty feet away and dry. On Tuesdays the kiln runs all morning in the room next door. A kiln pushes damp air out through a vent above the art room door. The puddle sits directly under that vent. Mr. Shaw taped a paper towel to the vent and it was soaked by noon.
cases.question: Where is the puddle coming from?

suspects.why: the kiln runs Tuesdays and the puddle sits under the vent
the roof was replaced and does not leak
forty feet away and dry

cases.answer: Damp air from the kiln vent drips onto the floor.
proof: “A kiln pushes damp air out through a vent above the art room door.”
“The puddle sits directly under that vent.”
clears: A roof leak: “The roof above it was replaced in August and does not leak.”
The fountain: “The drinking fountain is forty feet away and dry.”
cases.explain: A paper towel taped to the vent was soaked by noon. Because the kiln runs on Tuesdays and pushes damp air through that vent, the puddle shows up under it on Tuesdays only.

cases.title: The Case of the Headless Sunflowers
cases.story: The school garden grew twelve sunflowers and nine lost their heads overnight. The stalks are cut clean at an angle, not torn. The fence is four feet high and has no gaps. Deer tracks run along the outside of the fence and stop there. A deer can reach over a four-foot fence without jumping it. The three sunflowers that kept their heads grew in the middle of the bed. The nine that lost them all stood within arm's reach of the fence.
cases.question: What took the sunflower heads?

suspects.who: 🦌 A deer reaching over the fence
suspects.why: tracks outside the fence, and only the near flowers lost heads
the stalks are cut clean at an angle, not torn
the fence has no gaps

cases.answer: A deer reached over the fence and took them.
proof: “Deer tracks run along the outside of the fence and stop there.”
“A deer can reach over a four-foot fence without jumping it.”
clears: Insects: “The stalks are cut clean at an angle, not torn.”
Something getting through: “The fence is four feet high and has no gaps.”
cases.explain: The nine that lost their heads all stood within arm's reach of the fence, and the three in the middle kept theirs. Because the deer tracks stop at the outside of the fence and a deer can reach over four feet, it never had to come in.

cases.title: The Case of the Cold Nest
cases.story: A robin built a nest on the school ledge and sat on four eggs for nine days. On the tenth morning the robin was gone and the four eggs were cold. No shells lay on the ground and the nest was undamaged. The ledge is beside the gym door, which was propped open all week for painting. Workers walked past the nest about thirty times a day. Robins will abandon a nest that is disturbed too often. The week had been mild, with no night below fifty degrees.
cases.question: Why did the robin leave the nest?

suspects.why: workers passed thirty times a day, and robins abandon disturbed nests
no shells on the ground and the nest was undamaged
no night below fifty degrees

cases.answer: The robin abandoned the nest because people kept passing it.
proof: “Workers walked past the nest about thirty times a day.”
“Robins will abandon a nest that is disturbed too often.”
clears: A predator: “No shells lay on the ground and the nest was undamaged.”
Cold weather: “The week had been mild, with no night below fifty degrees.”
cases.explain: The eggs were still in the nest and nothing was broken, so nothing ate them. Because the gym door was propped open and workers passed about thirty times a day, the robin abandoned the nest.

cases.title: The Case of the Litter by the Gate
cases.story: The playground is clean except for one corner by the back gate. Wrappers pile up there every week. The nearest trash can sits by the basketball court, ninety feet away. The wind on this field blows steadily from the west. The back gate corner is the east fence line. Ms. Diaz emptied the corner on Monday and it had refilled by Friday without anyone eating there. Wind carries loose wrappers until a fence stops them. Nothing else on the playground catches them first.
cases.question: Why does litter collect in that one corner?

suspects.why: the wind blows from the west and the corner is the east fence line
it refilled without anyone eating there
the nearest can sits ninety feet away

cases.answer: The wind blows loose wrappers against the east fence.
proof: “The wind on this field blows steadily from the west.”
“Wind carries loose wrappers until a fence stops them.”
clears: Eating there: “it had refilled by Friday without anyone eating there.”
The trash can: “The nearest trash can sits by the basketball court, ninety feet away.”
cases.explain: The corner refilled in a week with nobody eating there. Because the wind blows steadily from the west and the back gate corner is the east fence line, wrappers travel across the field and stop at that fence.

cases.question: Why did eighty photographs come out black?

suspects.who: 🌑 No room light and no flash
suspects.why: the tank rooms are lit only by the tanks, and the flash was off
the camera battery was full
the lens was clean

proof: “The tank rooms are lit only by the tanks themselves.”
“A camera needs either light in the room or a flash.”
clears: The battery: “The camera battery was full.”
A dirty lens: “The lens was clean.”

cases.title: The Case of the Leaning Bean
cases.story: Two bean plants grew in identical cups on the same shelf. One stands straight and one leans hard to the left. Both got the same water and the same soil. The straight plant sits under the ceiling light. The leaning plant sits two feet to the right of the window. Plants grow toward the strongest light they can reach. The leaning plant points directly at the window. Ms. Reed turned its cup around and in four days it had leaned the other way.
cases.question: Why does one bean plant lean?

suspects.why: it points at the window, and plants grow toward light
both got the same water and the same soil
turning the cup made it lean the other way instead

cases.answer: The plant leans toward the light from the window.
proof: “Plants grow toward the strongest light they can reach.”
“The leaning plant points directly at the window.”
clears: Water and soil: “Both got the same water and the same soil.”
A weak stem: “Ms. Reed turned its cup around and in four days it had leaned the other way.”
cases.explain: Turning the cup made the plant lean the other way within four days. Because plants grow toward the strongest light and this one points directly at the window, the window is what it is reaching for.

it was plugged in and its light came on
the first hundred cups were solid

“Warm air pours into a freezer whenever the lid is open.”
clears: The freezer being off: “The freezer was plugged in.”
Bad ice cream: “The first hundred cups, served before noon, were solid.”
cases.explain: The first hundred cups, served before noon, were solid. Because the lid was propped open with a scoop from noon onward, warm air poured in and the thermometer read twenty-two degrees.

suspects.why: direct sun from ten, and they popped between ten and twelve
no pins were in the room
nobody touched them

“Air inside a balloon expands as it warms.”
clears: A pin: “no pins were in the room.”

cases.explain: The balloons on the inside wall are still full, and the eleven popped between ten and twelve. Because the window side was in direct sun from ten o'clock, the air inside expanded and the rubber stretched until it split.
